hints: The numbers jump up and down. Look at every other number.
Write the 1st, 3rd and 5th numbers as one series: 2, 4, 6. Write the 2nd, 4th and 6th as another: 10, 20, 30.
The next number is the 7th, so it belongs to the series 2, 4, 6. That series adds 2 each time.

steps.action: Check the differences: 10 − 2 = 8, then 10 to 4 is a drop of 6. Up, then down.
steps.why: When the numbers go up, down, up, down, the list is often two series mixed together.

steps.action: Take the 1st, 3rd and 5th numbers: 2, 4, 6. The rule is +2.
Take the 2nd, 4th and 6th numbers: 10, 20, 30. The rule is +10.
The blank is the 7th number, so it belongs to the first series (2, 4, 6).
steps.why: The odd places (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th) belong to the first series.

steps.action: Apply its rule: 6 + 2 = 8. The answer is 8.

trapNotes.12: This doubles 6. The first series adds 2 each time: 2, 4, 6.
trapNotes.32: This adds 2 to 30. The +2 rule belongs to the first series, so add 2 to 6, not to 30.
trapNotes.40: This continues the second series (10, 20, 30). But the 7th number belongs to the first series: 2, 4, 6.
